{
  "rel": "name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

# GitHub can deliver one tag push more than once. Runs for a tag wait for each other, so a later
# run sees the release an earlier one published.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    name: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Use lockfile-compatible npm
        run: npm install --global npm@12.2.0
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Verify tag and package version
        run: |
          package_version=$(node --input-type=module -e 'import manifest from "./package.json" with { type: "json" }; process.stdout.write(manifest.version)')
          test "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "v$package_version"
      - name: Audit runtime dependencies
        run: npm audit --omit=dev
      - name: Verify package
        run: npm run package:check
      - name: Run static checks
        run: npm run check
      # The tagged commit passed tests and coverage in CI; Pit installs from the tagged source.
      - name: Inspect package contents
        run: npm pack --dry-run
      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        # A published release for this tag at this commit means an earlier run for the same push
        # finished; leave it unchanged. Any other existing release is an error.
        run: |
          if view=$(gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>&1); then
            tagged=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --jq .sha)
            if [ "$view" = "false" ] && [ "$tagged" = "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
              echo "::notice::Release $GITHUB_REF_NAME is already published at $GITHUB_SHA; leaving it unchanged."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "::error::Release $GITHUB_REF_NAME already exists (draft: $view) at $tagged, not at this run's $GITHUB_SHA."
            exit 1
          fi
          case "$view" in
            *"release not found"*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Could not check for an existing release: $view"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --verify-tag --title "pit $GITHUB_REF_NAME" --generate-notes
",
  "chg": "# Changelog

Notable changes to Pit are documented here. GitHub release notes remain the authoritative detailed record for each tagged release.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.36.2] - 2026-11-13

### Added

- `workspace.viewImage` works on pi-durable hosts such as pi-action, with the limits it has on Pi, and the image reaches the model (#365). The new `images` option of `createPitDurableExtension` takes an `ImageProcessor`, such as `createNodePhotonImages()` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/node`, to resize and convert images to the model's limits; without one, PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP images within the byte limit attach as they are. See [Images](docs/durable.md#images).

### Fixed

- On pi-durable hosts, images that `tools.*` calls return are attached to the result instead of reported as omitted, also from tools that declare an output schema, whose images were dropped without notice.

## [0.36.1] - 2026-11-13

### Changed

- The `typescript` tool's description shows how to label a call: a first line such as `// @pit: {"label": "Run the test suite with coverage enabled"}`. Providers that sample the tool input with Pit's grammar have no `label` argument, so their calls showed "Run workspace task" in the transcript; they now carry the model's label.

## [0.36.0] - 2026-11-12

### Changed

- On pi-durable hosts, Pit stops offering pi-durable's coding tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `powershell`) to the model by default, so the model sees `typescript` as on Pi, and `tools.*` no longer binds the file and shell tools that `workspace.*` and `shell.*` supersede. This changes what the model is offered on existing pi-action workflows. `allowedTools` in the user's and a trusted project's `pit.json` now applies there and keeps matching tools offered, and the new `hideTools` option of `createPitDurableExtension` replaces the hide list or turns hiding off with `false`. See [Tools the model sees](docs/durable.md#tools-the-model-sees).

## [0.35.1] - 2026-11-11

### Changed

- Pit formats `typescript` sources with `oxfmt` 0.77.0. Development uses `oxlint` 1.92.0 and `vitest` 5.1.0.

## [0.35.0] - 2026-11-11

### Added

- `session.*` on pi-durable hosts: `outline`, `inspectEntry`, `elide`, and `summarize` rewrite the conversation's context with pi-durable edits, and `setNote`/`notes` keep notes in a conversation document shown as the `pit_notes` section, which pi-durable re-sends after compaction and forks inherit. As on Pi, a change applies only if its call succeeds, after the current tool round with `when: "now"` and notes, and by default when the run answers, through an `afterRun` hook. See [Context editing and notes](docs/durable.md#context-editing-and-notes).
- `pit/durable` exports Pit's `typescript` tool for hosts built on `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, such as pi-action. `createPitDurableExtension({ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log })`, also exported as `createPiDurableExtension` and listed under `pi.durable` in `package.json`, returns an extension with the tool and prompt sections for its guidelines and the user and project function catalogs. Session functions are conversation entries, so a reopened Harness and forks keep them; nested `tools.*` calls go through the host's `executeTool()` and reach every other callable tool, including pi-durable's coding tools, and questions (`ui.*` and the confirmations `functions.*` asks for) work on asynchronous hosts: Pit answers them from a `ui.answer` entry in the conversation or posts them through the host's `ui.ask` and ends the turn, so nothing waits for a person. Interactive hosts can still pass blocking dialogs, during which the program deadline pauses. Project trust is off by default, project function promotion and removal ask through the host's dialogs (and fail without them), and `session.*`, `commands.*`, `models.set`, model requests, and `workspace.viewImage` report that they are unavailable. The entry loads without Pi's coding agent, Pi's TUI, or TypeBox, and `@earendil-works/pi-durable` is an optional peer dependency. See [Pit on pi-durable hosts](docs/durable.md).",

  "input": "import { programInputAdmitsString } from "../functions/source.js";

/**
 * Some clients deliver the `params` tool argument as a JSON string. Decode a string that holds a
 * JSON object or array when the program's declared input cannot accept a string; otherwise pass
 * the value through unchanged so validation reports any mismatch against the declared type.
 */
export function resolveToolInput(source: string, params: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof params !== "string" || programInputAdmitsString(source) !== false) return params;
  const text = params.trim();
  if (!(text.startsWith("{") || text.startsWith("["))) return params;
  try {
    // Text that starts with { or [ can only parse to an object or array.
    return JSON.parse(text) as unknown;
  } catch {
    return params;
  }
}

const OPTIONAL_ARGUMENTS = ["label", "functionId", "params", "saveOnly", "timeoutMs"] as const;

/**
 * Treats a `null` optional tool argument as omitted. A provider sampling arguments against a strict
 * JSON schema must send every property, so it sends `null` for options the model left out. Pi drops
 * such a `null` only where the property's schema rejects it, which excludes `params`. `code` is
 * required, so a `null` there is left for validation to report.
 */
export function omitNullArguments<T>(args: T): T {
  if (typeof args !== "object" || args === null) return args;
  const record = args as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!OPTIONAL_ARGUMENTS.some((name) => record[name] === null)) return args;
  const result = { ...record };
  for (const name of OPTIONAL_ARGUMENTS) {
    if (result[name] === null) delete result[name];
  }
  return result as T;
}
"
}
